newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil confirms groups qualified for B Band bid.
newsitem.headline: Brazil confirms groups qualified for B Band bid.

text.p: Brazil's Communications Ministry distributed the following list confirming the names of consortia qualified to bid for concessions to operate cellular services on the Band B frequency.
Area One, Sao Paulo city -- Avantel, Brascom, TT2, Telet, BCP and GFTT.
Area Two, Sao Paulo state -- Avantel, Brascom, TT2, Telet, BCP and Global Telecom.
Area Three, Rio de Janeiro and Espirito Santo states -- Avantel, Brascom, TT2, Telet, BCP and GFTT.
Area Four, Minas Gerais state -- Avantel, Brascom, Telet, BCP, Vicuhna telecomunicacoes and Global telecom.
Area Five, Parana and Santa Catarina states -- Avantel, Brascom, Telet, BCP, GFTT, Vicunha Telecomunicacoes and Global Telecom.
Area Six, Rio Grande do Sul state -- Avantel, Brascom, Telet, BCP, Vicuhna Telecomunicacoes and Global Telecom.
Area Seven, center-west Brazil, including capital Brasilia, Goias state, plus Amazonian states of Acre, Rondonia and Tocantins -- Americel.
Area Eight, the rest of the north region (Amazonas, Roraima, Amapa and Maranhao states) -- No bidders.
Area Nine, Bahia and Sergipe states -- Avantel, BSE, Americel and Vicunha Telecomunicacoes.
Area Ten, the rest of the northeast (Ceara, Rio Grande do Norte, Paraiba, Pernambuco, Alagoas and Piaui states) -- Avantel, GFTT, BSE, Americel and Vicunha Telecomunicacoes.
Five consortia out of 15 that presnted bids in early April did not qualify for any areas. They were Lightel, Hutchison/Cowan, MCOM Wireless, Tess and Algar.
Those disqualifed have five working days to appeal to the Communications Ministry, after which the government expects to announce the winning bidders.
A spokesman said the ministry would begin by annoucing the winners for areas one and seven.
The Consortia:

* Avantel Comunicacoes Pessois, made up of Brazilian construction giants Odebrecht and Camargo Correa, Unibanco bank and AirTouch Communications of the United States. It has sumbitted bids for areas 1-6 and 9-10.
* Brascom -- construction firm Andrade Gutierrez, industrial group Monteiro Aranha (both Brazil), Southwestern Bell (U.S.) and cellular operator Mannesmann Eurokom (Germany). Areas 1-6.
* Lightel -- private telecoms operator Lightel, construction firm Queirroz Galvao (both Brazil), and Korean Mobile Telecom. Areas 5, 6 and 10.
* Hutchinson/Cowan -- telecommunications group Hutchinson Whampoa (Hong Kong) and construction company Cowan Construtora (Brazil). Areas 4, 5.
* MCOM Wireless -- The investment wing of Banco Garantia, Garantia Participacoes (Brazil), Telmex (Mexico), Comcast Corp (U.S.). Area 3.
* TT-2 Telecomunicacoes -- Bradesco bank and Globo Participacoes, the investment arm of the Globo media empire (both Brazil), AT&T and Stet. Areas 1, 2 and 3.
* Tess -- telecom operator Telia (Sweden), Airline Cellular (Brazil), and Primave, part of construction group C.R. Alameida (Brazil). Areas 1-6, 9-10.
* Telet -- pension funds, publically owned Banco do Brasil, Opportunity bank (Brazil), Bell Canada (a unit of BCE . Areas 1, 3, 5 and 10.
* BCP S.A. -- BellSouth Corp (U.S.), media group Estado de Sao Paulo, Banco Safra (Brazil), Splice. Areas 1-6.
* GFTT S.A. -- France Telecom, telecomunications venture Teldin (Brazil) and private equity funds of Banco Garantia. Areas 1, 3, 5 and 10.
* Algar -- same as Lightel consortium. Area 3.
* BSE S.A. -- same as BCP SA Areas 9, 10.
